correctness.rationale: The infinite lattice process exists by summable decreasing-time dependency paths. An exact half-line cavity Volterra system gives h_A=1-b. A discrepancy from switching the initially occupied root color can reach site d only along the unique time-increasing, alternating-color path, and an A difference survives at the endpoint precisely if the exterior cavity has no earlier B. Its probability is the explicit integral (1), with no competing negative A branch. Strict positivity follows from h_A>=1-beta*t>0, the sharp factorial coefficient from beta-kernel concentration, and the entire generating function and balanced t/2 sum from absolutely summing even/odd paths. Exhaustive finite-path rational checks, independent of the infinite formula, passed 252 parameter-and-site comparisons over 1,146,655 marked-order cases; nonfinite conclusions rely on analytic proof.

originality.rationale: An all-distance, color-specific response to an externally preoccupied opposite-color root, its sharp factorial coefficient, and a balanced full-half-line sum rule are not the unperturbed densities, all-A cylinder probabilities, distance-two covariance or periodic finite-size averages in the inspected work. The one-neighbor cavity identity and the underlying one-attempt model are explicitly credited as known. Exact propagation through increasing-time alternating-color chains is verified independently, and searches of published records found no direct or logically stronger statement. This is best-knowledge originality with a residual possibility of unindexed causal-influence results.
residual_risks: A previously unindexed pinned-seed or causal-influence result could subsume the claimed exact response.
The half-line cavity ODE and d=1 response are already covered and are used as premises rather than independent novelty.
Full text of Penrose-Sudbury 2005 was not inspected; its graphical generality is acknowledged but its stated models differ.
No independent publication-priority assessment or external mathematical validation was undertaken.

value.rationale: Seeding with one permanently occupied nucleus is a natural boundary/initial-condition perturbation of antagonistic deposition. Its effect on an arbitrary distant color density is not determined by published unseeded marginal densities or pair covariances. The theorem gives the complete, strictly signed spatial Green kernel, an exact sharp factorial screening coefficient and a closed all-distance susceptibility sum. These quantify the spatial range and cumulative response of a single competing-color nucleus; no general downstream theorem is needed for this natural, nonlocal response invariant.
